carries this lean against the challenger in those 7 debates.
  - THE PRESS LEDGER COUNTS AND LABELS ONLY THE PRESSED VERSES, AND READS A QUOTATION TO THE END OF ITS LINE (ASK 651 and ASK 652; D4 Build, Panel Build and Build Independent Verdict; for ASK 651 also the Shared Library PRS source):
    - The PROVEN IN check (PRS refCheck, one line in four copies): to find whether the named round quotes the verse with its reference, it reads from the reference to the end of that line. The quotation test is unchanged: a quotation that opens after the reference and closes on that line, or one that closes just before the reference. A quotation with no closing mark on its line still fails, and a verse named but not quoted still reads "the verse is named there but not quoted with its reference".
    - The premise reader (three copies; the Shared Library reader already takes its verses from PRS.premise): when PRS.premise has classed the premise, a reference in the PRESSED WITH block that is neither one of its pressed verses nor one of its presses past the cap is passed over: it is not counted as a press, not counted toward the cap of 8 pressed verses, and not labelled UNPROVEN. That covers the [L3] verse of a press line and a verse inside its MEANS. A press past the cap still reads "over the cap of 8 pressed verses". References the premise names before its PRESSED WITH block are listed as "other verses the premise names (informational, not witnesses)". When PRS gives no class for the premise, the reader works as before.
    - What reads the result: D4 Build's list of unproven presses given to the defender before its close, and the press ledger that Panel Build and Build Independent Verdict give the judges. Ruling 398, the cap and the WALL-2024 floor are unchanged; no prompt wording, model setting or reasoning is changed.
    - Not shown by a run. Mark for the next run: in the ledger a verse whose quotation in the named round is whole on its line reads PROVEN BY REFERENCE, and no [L3] or MEANS verse is listed as a press or as UNPROVEN.
